$comment: MONEY-979 T12 — the ONE recorded contract for the US coverage gate.
Two implementations compute this gate: judge_coverage() in
computing one gate is exactly how they drift, so both are pinned HERE:
Each test drives its REAL implementation over `filers` and asserts the
result equals `expected`. Neither restates the rule — this file is the
expected OUTPUT, not a third copy of the arithmetic. Change `expected`
only when the gate's definition changes, and change it in one commit with
both implementations; a value edited to make a test pass has silently
This file is NOT generated. Do not add a script that rewrites it: a
snapshot regenerated from one side is a snapshot that agrees with
whichever side ran last, which is the drift it was meant to catch.
Percentages are IEEE-754 doubles and round-trip exactly through JSON in
both languages; the tests still compare them with a 1e-9 tolerance so a
future case with a repeating fraction does not become a formatting test.

cases.name: empty
cases.why: The empty-population guard. 100, never NaN — `NaN >= 95` is false and so is `NaN < 95`, so a threshold check written either way reports the wrong thing without erroring. A caller that needs to tell 'vacuously satisfied' from 'measured 100%' reads `eligible === 0`.

cases.name: all_eligible_covered
cases.why: The healthy case: every eligible filer holds 5+ fiscal years.

cases.name: eligible_partial
cases.why: A real gap: 3 of 4 eligible filers are covered. 75, not 100.

cases.name: spac_batch
cases.why: THE case this gate exists for, and the one that dies first if the denominator is replaced by all filers. Two eligible filers, both covered; eight SPACs listed last year holding the single year each of them has. The gate is 100 because we hold everything obtainable. Over ALL filers it would read 20% and fail a release for a market condition no engineering can change. DO NOT DELETE THIS CASE — the gate tests assert it by name.

cases.name: ineligible_missing_years
cases.why: An ineligible filer that is NOT satisfied: SEC shows 3 fiscal years, we hold 1. The gate is unmoved (it is eligible-only, and correctly so) but overallPct drops to 50 — which is the only place this filer is visible at all. Without overallPct, 'the ineligible ones are fine too' would be an assumption.

cases.name: ineligible_zero_years
cases.why: A filer SEC shows zero fiscal years for is COMPLETE — there is nothing to fetch. `held >= atSec` with both at 0 is satisfied, and it must not be dragged into the gate as a failure.

cases.name: boundary_exactly_target
cases.why: The comparison is `>=`, so exactly 5 fiscal years is COVERED and 4 is not. An off-by-one here moves a release gate silently across the whole universe.

cases.name: dirty_inputs
cases.why: Coercion parity across the two languages. A numeric STRING is a number ('6' -> 6). null and a non-numeric string are NO VALUE and floor to 0, never silently becoming a count. A negative year count clamps to 0 rather than subtracting from the population. `eligibleForCoverage: 1` is NOT boolean true — TS tests `=== true` and Python tests `is True`, so this row is INELIGIBLE in both; anything looser would let a truthy non-boolean into the gate's denominator.

cases.name: repeating_fraction
cases.why: 2 of 3 is 66.666…, which is why both tests compare percentages with a tolerance instead of by string.
